reply_text:
I read this candidate as **borderline**. The quoted words are on the page, but whether they count as a prediction about AI (part 2 of the rule) is unclear, and under the rule a truly borderline case stays out.

**Page check.** The page opened. Some of the article is behind a sign-in, but this passage was readable. The sentence appears word for word: "That's the motivation for proposing an alternative to the natural course of things, which would be to leave the keys to this technology to the four companies that have captured most of the value of tech in the last 20 years and which, thanks to their dominant position, can largely capture most of the added value of the new industrial revolution that's coming in the next 20 years."

The page is The French Tech Journal's "Spotlight Interview: Mistral AI CEO Arthur Mensch" by Chris O'Brien, published 24 June 2024. It prints long excerpts of his testimony in English and says only that he "recently testified at the French Senate". It never gives the 22 May 2024 date; that comes from the search run and should be checked against the Senate's own record. Because it is an English rendering of his testimony, not a report about it, I'd treat it as a printed primary source, so part 4 is met.

**The four parts:**
1. **Role: met.** Mistral AI was founded in 2023, so by May–June 2024 he was its co-founder and chief executive.
2. **Looks forward and about AI: borderline.** "The new industrial revolution that's coming in the next 20 years" does look forward and is about AI. But it is a passing frame inside an argument about which companies will "capture most of the added value". That argument is about market share and value, which the rule treats as a business forecast. Nothing in it says what AI will do, reach or ship, and no outsider could test "an industrial revolution" by a date.
3. **Date or span: met.** "The next 20 years" is a span, which would make it due in 2044.
4. **Primary source: met**, as above.

**Already recorded?** No. The recorded claim from the same hearing date (2024-05-22, robots at human speed within five years) is a different claim.

If the person checking decides to admit it, I expect the test would be marked unfalsifiable, since "industrial revolution" has no stated test.
